name: West View Hotel — The Dining Room
why_it_matters: Heritage colonial bungalow on a six-acre plateau over the west valley — original gabled roofs, wooden ceilings, fireplaces and Raj-era furniture intact. Three dining venues (The Dining Room, Oak Garden Café, The Coffee Shop) serve Indian and continental fare with damask linen, German silver and china that have been on the property since the 1920s.
insider_tip: The Oak Garden Café is the move on a clear afternoon — pine-and-fir surround, valley sightlines, and the tea is properly brewed. Non-residents are welcome; call ahead for dinner so they set you a table indoors.
signature_address: Upper Mall Road, Ranikhet, Almora 263645, Uttarakhand

name: Chevron Rosemount — Restaurant
why_it_matters: Built by the British around 1900 and still hosting guests 125 years later — wrought iron grills, stone facade, vintage balconies, antiquated china and biblical paintings in the dining hall. Multi-cuisine kitchen handles Indian, continental, Mughlai and Chinese; the colonial atmosphere is the actual draw, the food is reliably above-average hill-station fare.
insider_tip: Walk-in non-resident diners are accommodated when the hotel isn't full — call ahead. Cantonment-area peace, 4 km from the bus stand, so plan a taxi back after dark.
signature_address: The Mall Road, Cantonment, Ranikhet, Almora 263645, Uttarakhand

name: Queen's Court — Ranikhet Club
why_it_matters: The dining hall of Ranikhet Club — the British-era institution founded in 1869 as a sanatorium and recreational club for the cantonment. Wooden floors, wooden ceiling, grand chandeliers, and a kitchen that has been feeding officers, planters and members for over 150 years. The Seven Peaks Bar adjoins it.
insider_tip: Non-members can apply for a temporary membership at the front desk to use the dining room and bar — usually granted same-day for travellers. Standards expected; no shorts at dinner.
signature_address: The Mall, Cantonment, Ranikhet, Almora 263645, Uttarakhand

name: Mayur Restaurant
why_it_matters: The most cited stop in Ranikhet for actual Kumaoni home cooking — aloo ke gutke (wok-fried potatoes with local spices), kafuli (fermented green-leaf curry), bhatt ki churkani (black soybean stew). Pure-veg, modest setting on the Almora road near Kalika Temple, four kilometres out of the cantonment.
insider_tip: Combine with a morning at Kalika Temple and the Jhula Devi temple loop — Mayur sits between them. They run thalis at lunch; à la carte gets slow on weekend afternoons.
signature_address: Almora-Ranikhet Road, near Kalika Temple, Ranikhet, Almora 263645, Uttarakhand

name: Moon Hotel & Restaurant
why_it_matters: Family-run since 1960 in the Ellias Building at Gandhi Chowk — the working-class restaurant in Sadar Bazaar's main chowk. Open through the day for breakfast, lunch, brunch, high tea and dinner. Not heritage in the colonial-bungalow sense, but a 65-year-old neighbourhood institution.
insider_tip: Use it for the breakfast paratha-and-tea routine if you're staying in Sadar Bazaar — it opens earlier than most Mall Road cafes and pulls a regular local crowd.
signature_address: Ellias Building, Gandhi Chowk, Sadar Bazaar, Ranikhet, Almora 263645, Uttarakhand

name: Dolia Pahadi The Roof Top Cafe
why_it_matters: Ranikhet's first rooftop café, atop the Almora Urban Bank building on Sadar Bazaar Road — a 270-degree open-terrace view of the Himalaya range. Indo-Chinese snacks, desserts, and live music on weekend evenings. The view is the product; the food is reasonable.
insider_tip: Go at sunset for the snow-line lighting up over Trishul and Nanda Devi; the kitchen slows down when the place fills, so order before the view does.
signature_address: Almora Urban Bank Building, Sadar Bazaar Road, Ranikhet, Almora 263645, Uttarakhand

name: The Coffee Cellar Bistro & Pizzeria
why_it_matters: Highway café about 19 km from Ranikhet town centre with a proper wood-fired pizza oven and two coffee-shop areas — uncommon for the Kumaon hills. Sits on an open ridge with mountain sightlines. Currently 5.0 on TripAdvisor, low review count but unanimous.
insider_tip: It's a road-trip stop, not a town café — make it part of the Kausani or Almora drive. Call ahead to confirm hours; small kitchen, runs out of pizza dough on busy weekends.

name: Hotel Parvati Inn — Restaurant
why_it_matters: Mid-range hotel restaurant on Mall Road with an in-house ice-cream parlour — a useful Mall Road option that isn't the heritage-tariff Chevron or West View. Standard north-Indian and Chinese, predictable rather than memorable, but reliably open and walk-in friendly.
insider_tip: Open to non-residents through the day; the ice-cream parlour pulls families in the evenings. Use as a fallback when the heritage hotels are booked out for events.
signature_address: Ratan Palace Compound, Mall Road, Ranikhet, Almora 263645, Uttarakhand
